sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Local Self Government** refers to the management of local affairs by such local bodies that have been elected by the local people.
Added via **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992**, introducing Part IX (Panchayats) and Part IX-A (Municipalities).
Pioneered in modern India by **Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882**, known as the **Magna Carta of Local Self Government**.
Enshrined under **Article 40** (Organisation of village panchayats) of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**.
First three-tier Panchayati Raj system was inaugurated by Prime Minister **Jawaharlal Nehru** on **2 October 1959** in **Nagaur district, Rajasthan**.
**Andhra Pradesh** adopted the Panchayati Raj system on **11 October 1959**.
**Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957)** recommended a **three-tier system**; Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a **two-tier system**.
High-scoring static GK area covering exact **Articles (243 to 243-ZG)**, schedules (**11th & 12th**), and committee names.

items.title: Evolution Committees and Their Recommendations
items.content:
• **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957):** Recommended **three-tier** Panchayati Raj (Gram Panchayat at village level, Panchayat Samiti at block level, Zila Parishad at district level).
• **Ashok Mehta Committee (1977):** Recommended **two-tier** system (Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat) and political party participation.
• **G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985):** Emphasized regular elections and called Panchayats **'grass without roots'**.
• **L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986):** Recommended **constitutional status** for Panchayati Raj institutions and judicial tribunals.
• **Mnemonic for Committees:** **'B'**alwant **'A'**shok **'G'**aneshlal **'L'**axmi (**BAG-L**: Balwant, Ashok, G.V.K., L.M. Singhvi).

items.title: Constitutionalization: 73rd and 74th Amendments
items.content:
• **73rd Amendment Act, 1992:** Added **Part IX**, Articles **243 to 243-O**, and the **11th Schedule** containing **29 functional items**.
• **74th Amendment Act, 1992:** Added **Part IX-A**, Articles **243-P to 243-ZG**, and the **12th Schedule** containing **18 functional items**.
• **Assent Dates:** Both acts came into force on **24 April 1993** (73rd) and **1 June 1993** (74th).
• **National Panchayati Raj Day:** Celebrated annually on **24 April**.
• **Mnemonic for Schedules:** **'11'** players play cricket in a **Village** (11th Schedule = 29 items for Villages); **'12'** months make a year in the **City** (12th Schedule = 18 items for Cities).

items.title: Three-Tier Structure of Panchayati Raj
items.content:
• **Gram Panchayat:** Operates at the **village level**; executive body headed by **Sarpanch / Pradhan**.
• **Panchayat Samiti:** Operates at the **block level / intermediate level**; acts as a link between Gram Panchayat and Zila Parishad; headed by **Pramukh**.
• **Zila Parishad:** Operates at the **district level**; advisory, coordinating, and supervisory body; headed by **Zila Panchayat Chairperson**.
• **Exempted Areas:** 73rd Amendment does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and certain scheduled areas (covered separately under **PESA Act, 1996**).

items.title: Types of Urban Local Bodies (74th Amendment)
items.content:
• **Nagar Panchayat:** For transitional areas (rural to urban transition).
• **Municipal Council (Municipal Board / Palika):** For smaller urban areas.
• **Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam):** For larger urban areas; headed by a **Mayor** with an administrative **Municipal Commissioner** (IAS officer).
• **Other Forms:** Cantonment Board, Township, Notified Area Committee, and Special Purpose Agency.

items.title: Reservation, Tenure, and Finance
items.content:
• **Reservation:** Mandatory **1/3rd (33%) reservation** for women across all tiers; reservation for SC/ST proportional to their population.
• **Tenure:** Fixed **5-year term** for all local bodies; fresh elections must be held before term expiry or within **6 months** in case of dissolution.
• **Minimum Age:** **21 years** is the minimum age to contest elections for local bodies.
• **State Finance Commission:** Constituted every **5 years** by the Governor to review financial positions (Article **243-I** and **243-Y**).

items.definition: Remember **21 for Local, 25 for Lok Sabha/Assembly, 30 for Rajya Sabha/Council**. For local bodies (Panchayat/Municipality), the minimum age is **21 years**.
Think of **9** as a **Village Hut** (Part IX = Panchayats) and **9A** as a **City Apartment** attached to it (Part IX-A = Municipalities).
11th Schedule has **29 items** (2 + 9 = 11, matching schedule number). 12th Schedule has **18 items** (1 + 8 = 9, reverse of 6, or think of 18 as the legal age of adulthood in cities).
Use the acronym **GPZ**: **G**ram Panchayat (Village), **P**anchayat Samiti (Block), **Z**ila Parishad (District).
Use the acronym **NMMC**: **N**agar Panchayat (Small), **M**unicipality (Medium), **M**unicipal **C**orporation (Large).

items.term: Trick 6: Father of Local Self Government
items.definition: Associate **'Ripon'** with **'Ribbon'** — local self-government was neatly tied up and presented as a gift by **Lord Ripon in 1882**.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing 73rd and 74th Amendment Years with Enforcement Years
items.definition: Both acts were passed in **1992**, but they came into force in **1993** (24 April 1993 for 73rd and 1 June 1993 for 74th).

items.term: Mistake 2: Confusing Balwant Rai Mehta with Ashok Mehta Committee
items.definition: Balwant Rai Mehta = **3 tiers** (1957). Ashok Mehta = **2 tiers** (1977). Students often mix up the number of tiers recommended by each.

items.term: Mistake 3: Confusing Minimum Age for Voting vs Contesting
items.definition: Voting age is **18 years** (reduced by 61st Amendment, 1988), but contesting local body election age is **21 years**.

items.term: Mistake 4: Assuming PESA Act applies to all states
items.definition: PESA Act (**1996**) applies only to **Scheduled Areas** under Fifth Schedule, not to all states or Sixth Schedule areas.

items.term: Mistake 5: Confusing State Finance Commission and Central Finance Commission
items.definition: State Finance Commission is constituted under **Article 243-I (for Panchayats)** and **243-Y (for Municipalities)** by the Governor, NOT the President.

items.term: Mistake 6: Confusing Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat
items.definition: **Gram Sabha** consists of all registered voters in a village, while **Gram Panchayat** is the smaller executive body elected by the Gram Sabha.
**Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882** is hailed as the **Magna Carta** of local self-government in India.
Provided via **73rd (Panchayats)** and **74th (Municipalities) Amendment Acts, 1992**.
Part **IX** & **11th Schedule** (Panchayats); Part **IX-A** & **12th Schedule** (Municipalities).
First implemented in **Nagaur, Rajasthan** on **2 October 1959** by Jawaharlal Nehru.
Three-tier Panchayati Raj system: **Gram Panchayat**, **Panchayat Samiti**, and **Zila Parishad**.
Three types of urban local bodies: **Nagar Panchayat**, **Municipal Council**, and **Municipal Corporation**.
Fixed **5-year term** with mandatory elections conducted by the **State Election Commission**.
Mandatory **not less than 33% (1/3rd)** reservation for women in all local bodies.
State Finance Commission is established every **5 years** under **Article 243-I**.
**District Planning Committee (DPC)** consolidates plans prepared by panchayats and municipalities.
Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and hill areas of Manipur are exempted from Part IX.
Enacted in **1996** to extend provisions of Part IX to Scheduled Areas with tribal self-rule focus.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks exact article numbers related to Panchayats (Articles 243 to 243-O) and Municipalities (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG). Memorize the starting and ending articles for both.
Focus heavily on the committees and their chronological order: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) -> Ashok Mehta (1977) -> G.V.K. Rao (1985) -> L.M. Singhvi (1986).
Questions often trap students by asking who appoints the State Finance Commission. Remember it is the **Governor of the State**, NOT the President of India.
Do not confuse the number of subjects in the 11th Schedule (**29 items**) with the 12th Schedule (**18 items**). Always verify rural vs. urban context.

keyTakeaways: Local self-government is enshrined under **Article 40** (DPSP) and institutionalized via **73rd and 74th Amendments, 1992**.
Lord Ripon is recognized as the **Father of Local Self Government** in colonial India (1882).
Rajasthan was the **first state** to establish the Panchayati Raj system in **Nagaur** on **2 October 1959**.
The 11th Schedule contains **29 functional items** for Panchayats, while the 12th Schedule contains **18 items** for Municipalities.
Minimum age to contest elections to local bodies is **21 years**.
Mandatory **one-third (33%) reservation** for women is a key feature of both amendments.
The **State Election Commission** conducts elections to all local bodies independently.
